In addition, the organization delivers direct community assistance by operating a <cite id="3">monthly food pantry and life skills support</cite> for low-income and refugee families.
rich_narrative.summary: Islamic Oasis presents significant financial allocation concerns that limit its overall effectiveness. In FY2024, the organization reported a <cite id="3">total revenue of $4,794,010</cite>, yet recorded a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 4.8%</cite>. This is sharply lower than the <cite id="1">peer program ratio median of 89.2%</cite> and the <cite id="1">75% industry benchmark</cite>. While the organization maintains direct services such as a <cite id="3">monthly food pantry and life skills training</cite> for low-income and refugee families, the vast majority of its financial output is not reflected in standard program expenditure. <cite id="1">Founded in 2008</cite>, Islamic Oasis operates emergency response, water projects, and masjid construction, with verified <cite id="2">zakat-eligible programs serving the poor and needy</cite>. Financial filings show strong liquidity, including <cite id="1">17.2 months of working capital</cite> and total assets of $5,726,976 in FY2024. However, severe gaps in board governance disclosures and an incomplete program expense breakdown represent primary limiting factors for potential supporters.
